verdict.rationale: Grok Build documents a permissions system with per-tool rules (e.g. a deny action keyed on tool and pattern) and an auto mode that only auto-approves safe tools. Integrations are explicitly configured MCP servers added via `grok mcp add`, and `grok inspect` shows which MCP servers were discovered, so the lead can govern which external tools are present. However, the evidence only shows rule examples for bash, not allow/deny rules scoped to MCP servers or plugin tools, and nothing on team-wide or managed policy enforcement. missing for 10: documented allow/deny rules for specific MCP/integration tools, centrally managed or team-enforced policy, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can control which external tools and integrations the agent is allowed to access

citations.quote: Classifier auto-approves safe tools; dangerous ones may still prompt
MCP servers expose external tools to Grok. Once configured, their tools are available alongside the built-in ones
use `grok inspect` to see what Grok discovered in the current directory, including config sources, instructions, skills, plugins, hooks, and MCP servers
